title: Double-counit identification in an etale-horizontal square
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring and let
$$\begin{array}{ccc}R'&\xrightarrow{e'}&R\\ h'\downarrow&&\downarrow h\\ T'&\xrightarrow e&T\end{array}$$
be a Cartesian square of Noetherian schemes, meaning schemes admitting finite affine covers by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. Assume every arrow is separated and finite type, the horizontal arrows $e,e'$ are etale, and give the arrows and their equal composites $he'=eh'$ compactifications [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Work in ordinary unbounded small-etale constant-$A$ module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Write $F_a=Ra_!\dashv G_a$ with counit $\varepsilon_a$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support, thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. For $a=e,e'$, put $S_a=D(a_{\Sigma!})\dashv a^*$ with evaluation $\operatorname{ev}_a$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension, lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality], take $d_a:F_a\xrightarrow{\sim}S_a$ from the proper-support/sum comparison [lem-sfb-quasifinite-compact-support-exact], and put $\rho_a=(d_a^{-1})^c:G_a\xrightarrow{\sim}a^*$ [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate]. Let $\alpha_{b,a}:F_bF_a\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{ba}$ and $C:e^*F_h\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{h'}e'^*$ be the specified compact-support compositor and exchange [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons], and let $c_{b,a}:G_{ba}\xrightarrow{\sim}G_aG_b$ be the conjugate of $\alpha_{b,a}$ under the composite adjunction [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. Define
$$\delta=(d_eF_{h'})\alpha_{e,h'}^{-1}\alpha_{h,e'}F_h(d_{e'}^{-1}):F_hS_{e'}\xrightarrow{\sim}S_eF_{h'}.$$
For every $K\in D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ define the isomorphism
$$b_K=G_{h'}(\rho_{e,K})c_{e,h',K}c_{h,e',K}^{-1}\rho_{e',G_hK}^{-1}:e'^*G_hK\longrightarrow G_{h'}e^*K.$$
Writing $t_K=\varepsilon_{h,K}$ and $t'_K=\varepsilon_{h',e^*K}$, its composite counit satisfies the equality of maps $S_eF_{h'}e'^*G_hK\to K$
$$\operatorname{ev}_{e,K}\circ S_e(t'_K\circ F_{h'}b_K)=t_K\circ F_h(\operatorname{ev}_{e',G_hK})\circ\delta_{e'^*G_hK}^{-1}.$$
Moreover its single counit is
$$t'_K\circ F_{h'}b_K=e^*(t_K)\circ C_{G_hK}^{-1}:F_{h'}e'^*G_hK\longrightarrow e^*K.$$
Thus $b_K$ is exactly the $F_{h'}\dashv G_{h'}$ adjunct of the displayed inverse-exchange/counit composite. These equalities hold for the specified maps, are natural in $K$, and commute with proper-refinement comparisons and further compatible Cartesian open restriction; right-adjoint restriction comparisons here are those determined by the compact-support exchange and the same normalized sum/evaluation adjunctions. No smoothness or purity assertion is assumed.
